c74object.name: tap.gardener
c74object.digest: The idle wind that plants the garden when you stop
c74object.description: The tap.gardener object is the self-seeding half of tap.garden~. After idle seconds with nobody planting, it starts planting for you: strikes arrive on a calm and gust cycle, where gust sizes the clusters — up to five neighbouring tubes within a fraction of a second — with the calms between them stretched so the average rate stays near one strike per loop pass at any setting. It is wind, not a sequence. The random stream is drawn from only while idling, which is what makes seed a contract: the same seed gives the same wind every run, a different seed decorrelates two instances, and with idle 0 the seed cannot matter at all because the stream is never touched. Pitches come out raw and unquantized on purpose — the scale is the patch's field, not the wind's, so put tap.scale after it.

inlet.digest: planted or bang — close the idle gate, something else just planted.

method.name: planted
method.description: Close the idle gate: something else just planted, so the wind drops and waits out another idle period before it starts again.

method.name: clear
method.description: Re-seed the random stream and restart both the idle clock and the wind.

attribute.name: idle
attribute.description: Seconds of quiet before the wind picks up. 0 disables it entirely — and then the seed cannot matter, because the random stream is never consumed.

attribute.name: gust
attribute.description: The wind, 0 to 1. At 0 strikes arrive singly and evenly, about one per pass; up from there they cluster into gusts with longer calms between, at the same average rate.

attribute.name: seed
attribute.description: The wind's seed. Same seed, same wind, every run — so a render reproduces, and two instances decorrelate by seeding them differently.

attribute.name: loop
attribute.description: The loop length in seconds this wind is blowing across — match it to the tap.bloom it feeds. It sizes the gusts and the calms.

attribute.name: interval
attribute.description: Scheduler tick in milliseconds (0.1 to 100) — both how often the wind is advanced and its time resolution. Changing it re-seeds and restarts the wind.
